title: What the live paper record shows
description: The engines' own state, read from the running record: what is open, what closed, and what the market filter is doing right now.
body:
Every position in this record is paper. No real orders are placed anywhere in it. A single trade, or a short sequence of trades, says nothing about a strategy. The figures below are the engines' own state read from the running record at the stated snapshot time, and the record updates continuously.

## Open positions
htf-rsi-v007 shows 0 positions open on paper. trend-daily-v005 shows 0 positions open on paper. trend-daily-v006 shows 0 positions open on paper. The record also notes a NEAR entry at 5.896 on 12 October 2026 that has been open since that date. An open position is one that has been entered and not yet exited under the engine's rules, so the NEAR entry is not part of any closed-trade average. Because the live record is short, an empty book is a state, not a verdict. The open count is measured directly from the running record, and it can change as new signals arrive. The NEAR entry remains open, so its eventual result is not yet reflected in any average. The engines named above each report 0 open positions, while the NEAR position sits outside those counts as an open entry recorded in the log.

## Closed trades
htf-rsi-v007 has 4 closed trades so far, with an average null net per trade. trend-daily-v005 has 6 closed trades so far, with an average -13.22% net per trade. trend-daily-v006 has 7 closed trades so far, with an average -13.34% net per trade. The first live signal was an ATOM entry at 2.066 after the 10 October 2026 daily close. ATOM exited below its 10-day low at the 18 October 2026 close, at 1.703, which is -17.9% after the 30 bps round trip. The ATOM result is a single completed trade, and its -17.9% outcome is already reflected in the averages where that trade was recorded. The closed-trade averages combine all completed trades for each engine, so they include the ATOM loss where that engine recorded it. A negative average after a small number of trades is consistent with a process that expects losses to occur more often than wins. The null average for htf-rsi-v007 means the engine's record does not show a percentage average for its 4 closed trades, not that the result is zero.

## Market filter
The Bitcoin market filter is off for trend-daily-v005 and trend-daily-v006. With the filter off, both engines show 0 positions open on paper. The record also lists the names closest to a 20-day breakout. For trend-daily-v005: TRXUSDT is 13.39% below its high, ATOMUSDT is 18.95% below its high, and AAVEUSDT is 19.40% below its high. For trend-daily-v006: TRXUSDT is 13.39% below its high, JUPUSDT is 14.56% below its high, and ATOMUSDT is 18.95% below its high. The proximity percentages are distances below the high, so a smaller percentage means a market is closer to its 20-day breakout level. The filter state is a live condition, not a forecast. When it is off, the record shows no open trend positions for those engines, and the proximity list shows how far the named markets are from their 20-day highs. Those distances are measurements from the record, not entry signals. The fact that ATOMUSDT appears in both lists with the same distance reflects the same underlying measurement recorded for both engines.

## Reading the losing start
v005 counts its live record from 1 October 2026 and v006 from 9 October 2026. The live start has produced losses: ATOM closed at -17.9% after the 30 bps round trip, and the closed-trade averages for v005 and v006 are negative. In testing, losses were common and the average winner was roughly +19%, so a losing start is the expected case rather than a surprise. The +19% figure is an average winner from testing, not a target or an expectation for any individual trade. One trade, or a short sequence, does not validate or invalidate a strategy; the record is paper and remains short. The expectation comes from prior testing, while the live record is the separate, shorter sample now being accumulated. Keeping those two samples distinct matters, because a short live record can differ from a longer test without implying that either is wrong.

## Where to check
The same numbers appear on the performance page, in the signal log, and in the status posted to the channel. The status posted to the channel is another copy of the same running record. This live snapshot was read at 2026-11-17T15:18:03.128Z. Because the record updates continuously, the counts, averages, filter state, and proximity distances can move after that time. Rechecking those locations is the way to see the current state rather than relying on this note. Nothing here recommends a trade, a coin, or a position size.
